macro.stance: Constructive industrial demand, but higher geopolitical oil risk and weakening consumer data argue for a barbell of physical-infrastructure beneficiaries and valuation discipline.
marketContext: On 2026-08-14 the S&P 500 closed 0.17% lower at 7,785.58 after recent record highs; elevated AI-linked valuations are increasingly being scrutinised.
Weak July U.S. retail-sales data and softer consumer sentiment reduced the immediate probability of a September Fed hike and pulled the dollar/yields lower during the session.
Brent rebounded toward the high-$80s as U.S.-Iran tensions and threats around Hormuz reintroduced a geopolitical risk premium after the prior inventory-driven pullback.

Texas data-centre grid-connection restrictions are a new location-specific risk for merchant generators and grid-dependent campuses, but reinforce the value of transmission investment and behind-the-meter/off-grid generation solutions.

ism.status: No new monthly release since the July 2026 Manufacturing and Services reports. Existing official July snapshot remains authoritative and was re-verified; no timestamp-only rewrite made.
ism.interpretation: Manufacturing re-acceleration, low customer inventories, strong backlog and persistent electrical/electronic bottlenecks remain supportive of grid equipment, power generation, electrical components and automation suppliers with pricing power. Services remains expansionary but shows hotter prices and softer employment.

categoryReads.change: Maintained; sharpened preference for equipment over merchant generation
categoryReads.why: GE Vernova's Q2 backlog/order evidence remains exceptional and the latest market development is Texas restricting new data-centre grid connections. That raises regulatory/location risk for some merchant generators while strengthening the case for transmission, substation, gas-turbine and off-grid power equipment.
actions: Maintain GEV and HUBB as priority equipment exposures
Maintain ETN/PWR and other T&D bottleneck names
Do not chase merchant generators solely on data-centre load assumptions; reassess Texas/PJM regulatory exposure name by name

categoryReads.why: AI demand remains strong, but Applied Materials' post-earnings weakness and broader scrutiny of AI-linked valuations show that good operating results are no longer sufficient for multiple expansion. Grid access is becoming a binding project constraint in Texas.
actions: Prefer electrical, power, cooling, networking and behind-the-meter infrastructure
Avoid adding duplicate high-multiple compute beta without a differentiated bottleneck

categoryReads.why: No new primary evidence today clears the bar for score changes. Structural power scarcity still supports nuclear operators, fuel-cycle suppliers and enrichment scarcity, but current valuations require selectivity.
actions: Maintain BWXT/CEG quality bias and LEU/CCJ fuel-cycle exposure

categoryReads.why: Oil rebounded on renewed U.S.-Iran/Hormuz tension even as the prior large U.S. inventory build and weaker demand signals cap the fundamental upside. The resulting two-sided market favours quality integrated producers, gas infrastructure and tactical refining rather than leveraged marginal upstream beta.
actions: Keep MPC/VLO tactical; do not capitalise current crack spreads as permanent

categoryReads.why: July ISM continues to flag copper, electronic components, memory and semiconductor constraints. The better risk-adjusted expression remains equipment/component suppliers with pricing power rather than undifferentiated commodity beta.

categoryReads.change: Humanoid evidence improved but hierarchy unchanged
categoryReads.why: Unitree's Shanghai IPO was reported more than 8,000x oversubscribed, confirming extreme investor demand and improving commercial credibility for humanoids. Nvidia/LG are also targeting a bipedal humanoid debut in early 2027. Neither changes the near-term adoption hierarchy because warehouse/fixed automation and cobots/mobile manipulation have clearer deployed economics today.
actions: Maintain SYM, Geekplus, CGNX and TER ahead of humanoid OEMs
Do not promote Unitree at scarcity-driven IPO valuation

categoryReads.why: No fresh company-specific evidence today clears the materiality bar. Existing preference remains for electrical/cable, power and construction exposures that monetise committed projects rather than speculative data-centre announcements.
actions: Maintain Southern Cable/YTL Power and established infrastructure queue
No new Bursa name promoted today

categoryReads.change: Robotics enthusiasm increased; valuation risk increased with it
categoryReads.why: Physical-AI investor appetite is exceptionally strong around Unitree while China's AI/hardware ecosystem remains active. Prefer listed names with existing revenues and sensible entry valuation over scarcity-driven humanoid IPO exposure.
actions: Maintain Geekplus and existing nuclear/power exposures
No new HK/China stock promoted today

companyChanges.reason: Latest Q2 evidence remains thesis-defining: $24.2bn orders (+88% organic), $176bn backlog, 116 GW of gas equipment commitments and >$5bn YTD data-centre orders. Shares rose again on Aug. 14, so valuation/position sizing remains the restraint rather than fundamentals.
No contradictory evidence since promotion. Utility T&D book-to-bill and data-centre-driven transmission/substation quoting remain differentiated exposure to the grid bottleneck.

Texas data-centre connection restrictions and evolving PJM capacity procurement/co-location rules raise uncertainty around the speed and pricing of merchant-power monetisation. Do not broadly downgrade yet, but direct-contract/off-grid capability now deserves more weight.

researchedNotPromoted.reason: Solar Turbines is benefiting from off-grid/data-centre turbine demand, but Caterpillar is diversified enough that the Power Stack signal is diluted relative to GEV and dedicated grid/power names.
Gas-turbine and energy-security exposure is improving, but existing gas infrastructure and GEV exposure capture the current theme more directly.
Commercial humanoid evidence is improving, but extreme IPO oversubscription/scarcity and valuation risk fail the entry-quality bar.
